text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Home affairs minister Chitalu Sampa directs the police command to instantly dismiss policemen found drinking on duty.
- The ruling Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) reclaims three parliamentary seats unchallenged after opposition parties boycott by-elections scheduled for May 28.
- The Central Statistics Office says the level of poverty in Zambia has dropped to around 69 percent from 76 percent.
- Air France to start a commercial freight service to Zambia before year-end.

- Former foreign affairs minister Vernon Mwaanga asks the Lusaka high court to review an order that he pay 10,000 pounds sterling as security for costs before a libel suit he has taken against Newsweek International can start.
- An initial public offer of 13 million Zambian Breweries shares which opened three weeks ago closes on Wednesday.
- The farmers union says Zambia is unlikely to benefit from rising world cereal prices because her bad geographical position and poor infrastructure are not favourable for the export trade.
